skill.name: c4-modeling

content.value_statement: Architecture discussions become confusing when diagrams mix detail levels or omit relationships. This skill creates structured C4 views and reviews them against consistent guidelines.
actual_capabilities: Creates context, container, component, and selective code-level C4 views from supplied architecture details.
Organizes people, systems, containers, components, boundaries, technologies, and labeled relationships.
Produces Mermaid C4 syntax using documented elements, relationships, directions, boundaries, and styles.
Guides transitions between C4 levels while preserving external systems and relevant context.
Reviews diagrams for mixed abstractions, missing descriptions, unlabeled relationships, unclear boundaries, and excessive detail.
limitations: Requires accurate architecture details from the user and does not discover deployed systems automatically.
Provides detailed syntax examples for Mermaid, but not equivalent references for Structurizr or PlantUML.
Offers conceptual Level 4 guidance without a dedicated code-diagram syntax reference.
Does not render, validate, publish, or automatically synchronize diagrams with source code.

use_cases.title: Plan a new system
use_cases.description: Build context and container views before selecting services, data stores, and integration boundaries.

use_cases.title: Align technical stakeholders
use_cases.description: Present consistent architecture views that separate business context from runtime and implementation details.

use_cases.title: Review an existing design
use_cases.description: Check diagrams for mixed levels, missing relationships, unclear responsibilities, and unnecessary detail.

prompt_templates.title: Create a context diagram
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Level 1 C4 context diagram for [system]. Include [users], [external systems], and labeled relationships. Ask for missing essential details.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a high-level view for technical and non-technical stakeholders.

prompt_templates.title: Expand into containers
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this approved context view, create a Level 2 container diagram for [system]. Show applications, services, data stores, queues, technologies, and relationships.
prompt_templates.scenario: Zoom into one system after its context and dependencies are established.

prompt_templates.title: Model container components
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Level 3 component diagram for [container]. Include major modules, responsibilities, repositories, integrations, boundaries, and connections to other containers.
prompt_templates.scenario: Document the internal structure needed by developers working on one container.

prompt_templates.title: Review and refine C4 views
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these C4 diagrams for abstraction mixing, omissions, unclear labels, and excessive detail. Return prioritized findings and revised Mermaid diagrams for each level.
prompt_templates.scenario: Conduct an advanced architecture review across several related diagrams.

output_examples.input: Create a context view for a clinic scheduling platform used by patients and staff.
output_examples.output: A Level 1 view centers the scheduling platform and connects patients, clinic staff, an identity provider, and a notification service with labeled relationships.

output_examples.input: Expand an online store into a container view using React, Node.js, PostgreSQL, Redis, and RabbitMQ.
output_examples.output: A Level 2 view separates the web application, API server, worker, database, cache, and queue while labeling technologies and communication paths.

output_examples.input: Review a diagram that combines users, databases, API modules, and classes.
output_examples.output: The review identifies mixed abstraction levels, recommends separate context, container, and component views, and assigns each element to the appropriate diagram.

best_practices: Start with a context diagram unless an approved higher-level view already exists.
State the audience and purpose before selecting the C4 level and included details.
Give every element a clear description and every relationship a meaningful label.
anti_patterns: Do not create a detailed container or component view before establishing system context.
Do not combine people, containers, components, classes, and functions in one diagram.
Do not invent dependencies, technologies, or responsibilities when the source information is incomplete.

faq.question: Which C4 level should I start with?
faq.answer: Start with Level 1 context unless a current, approved context diagram already exists.

faq.question: Can this skill create Mermaid diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Mermaid C4 syntax for elements, boundaries, relationships, complete examples, and optional styling.

faq.question: Does it support Structurizr or PlantUML?
faq.answer: The skill lists both formats, but its detailed syntax guidance and examples focus on Mermaid.

faq.question: Can it inspect my running system automatically?
faq.answer: No. Provide the actors, systems, technologies, dependencies, and responsibilities that the diagrams should represent.

faq.question: When should I use a code-level diagram?
faq.answer: Use Level 4 only for critical algorithms, key interfaces, complex data structures, or architecturally significant classes.

faq.question: How does it help with architecture reviews?
faq.answer: It checks level selection, abstraction consistency, descriptions, relationship labels, technology choices, element counts, and boundaries.
